evidence.fit_with_native_workflow: Adds a capability the project's current native stack (Claude Code Agent/Workflow tool, Codex CLI/exec) does not have: dispatch of a headless Claude Code agent from a GitHub event (issue comment, PR open, workflow_dispatch, or cron) with the run living entirely on a GitHub-hosted CI runner rather than inside a local Claude Code session. It reuses the same CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN concept the project's native Claude Code login already produces (via `claude setup-token`), so no new paid credential is strictly required, though an org-shared-secret setup recommends an API key instead (OAuth token is "tied to the subscription of the person who ran `claude setup-token`"). Isolation is CI-runner-per-run (C3-clean): no shared host state, and deterministic code (the workflow YAML, --allowedTools, settings.permissions.allow) owns the effects, matching the project's worktree/sandbox ownership model even though the isolation mechanism (ephemeral GitHub runner) differs from the project's local worktree/sandbox pattern.
evidence.interface: GitHub Action (`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`) wrapping the Claude Agent SDK. Two run modes selected automatically from workflow config: interactive mode (no `prompt` input — waits for an `@claude` mention in an issue/PR comment, PR review, or issue body/title) and automation mode (a `prompt` input — plain text or a `/skill-name` invocation — runs unconditionally on whatever GitHub event triggers the workflow, including `schedule`). CLI behavior/model/tool config is passed through via `claude_args` (accepts arbitrary Claude Code CLI flags: `--max-turns`, `--model`, `--mcp-config`, `--allowedTools`, `--debug`, etc.), and results surface either as an issue/PR comment or as workflow-run-log output plus validated JSON "structured outputs" wired into GitHub Action outputs.
evidence.isolation_model: Runner-per-invocation: each trigger spins up a fresh GitHub-hosted (or self-hosted) Actions runner with `actions/checkout` providing a scoped repo copy; no persistent host state carries between runs. Tool access is deny-by-default — Bash/arbitrary shell is not granted unless explicitly allow-listed via `--allowedTools`/`settings.permissions.allow` — and a "Who can trigger runs" gate (write-access + human-actor checks) constrains which external events can start a run at all.

evidence.summary: Mission Control is a self-hosted, alpha-stage, SQLite-backed control plane (Web UI + CLI + MCP server + REST/WebSocket/SSE) for dispatching tasks to and reviewing/tracking spend across multiple agent runtimes (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, Claude SDK). Evidence confirms C1 (native-login reuse via a documented 'coexist' JSONL-sharing mode with the host Claude Code/Codex CLI, no new key required) and C4 (MIT license, tests/ dir, 8 active CI workflows including CodeQL/OSV-scanner/quality-gate, v2.3.0 released 2026-07-25, pushed today, 6252 stars). It also has a documented fallback requiring separate provider API keys, no documented per-task sandbox/worktree isolation (it is itself a standing server with shared DB state, weighing against C3), and directly overlaps the incumbent native Workflow tool + child-usage.mjs pairing on dispatch tracking and spend/usage accounting (C5). Given agreement-without-execution never promotes per the task rules, and no local comparison was run here, this is a keep_but_compare case: the named overturning comparison is whether Mission Control's dashboard/DB captures per-child model/effort/usage and run-review completeness at least as well as `node .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs --latest` plus the native Workflow tool on one identical wave — run entirely in coexist mode so no separate provider API key is introduced.

evidence.summary: A Microsoft-maintained Python CLI (`conductor-cli`, MIT, 454 stars, created 2026-02-02) that runs deterministic, version-controlled multi-agent workflows defined in YAML: named agents, Jinja2-templated conditional routing (first match wins, no LLM in the control loop), static/dynamic parallel groups, sub-workflow composition, script/set/MCP/terminate step types, human-in-the-loop gates, a Fleet Manager TUI, a real-time web dashboard with a live DAG, and OpenTelemetry tracing. It supports five interchangeable model providers: Copilot (stable, GitHub-auth, subscription), OpenAI (stable, API key), Claude via Pydantic AI (stable, requires a separate `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), Claude Agent SDK (experimental, authenticates via the `claude` CLI's own login, i.e. rides the native Claude Code sign-in, but has documented capability carve-outs), and NousResearch Hermes (experimental, API key). It also exposes registered workflows as MCP tools over stdio (`conductor mcp serve`) and can itself call MCP tools deterministically from a workflow step.
evidence.interface: CLI + YAML workflow definitions + web dashboard + Fleet Manager TUI; conductor also ships as an MCP server (`conductor mcp serve`, stdio-only in v1) that exposes each registered workflow as a typed MCP tool, and as an MCP client (`runtime.mcp_servers` / MCP steps) that workflows can call. `conductor run --silent` returns a single JSON result; `--web`/`--web-bg` start the dashboard. The `src/` tree is an installable Python package, but the documented, supported interface is the CLI/YAML/dashboard surface, not a documented embeddable Python SDK.
evidence.auth_model: Per-agent, set by `runtime.provider` in the workflow YAML or `--provider` on the CLI. Copilot provider: GitHub Copilot subscription/GitHub auth (stable tier). OpenAI provider: `OPENAI_API_KEY` (stable tier, pay-per-token). Claude provider (stable tier): delegates to Pydantic AI's `AnthropicModel`, requires the `anthropic` SDK and an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (docs/providers/claude.md §Quick Start: 'export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...') — this is a separate paid API key, not the Claude Code subscription login. Claude Agent SDK provider (experimental tier): docs/providers/comparison.md lists its Setup column as '`claude` CLI auth', i.e. it rides the already-installed native Claude Code CLI/subscription sign-in — but it is explicitly experimental with declared capability carve-outs (e.g. no per-agent tools allowlist) that `conductor validate` flags. Hermes provider: API key via OpenRouter-style setup. The ACA (Azure Container Apps) provider is a separate execution-location choice (not identity) requiring `az login`/`DefaultAzureCredential` for a 'Session Executor' role.
evidence.isolation_model: By default, workflow orchestration (routing, WorkflowContext, checkpoints, event bus) and each agent's agentic loop run in the host Conductor process — no per-workflow sandbox or worktree isolation is built in for the stable providers; running two workflows concurrently in the same repo checkout would share the CWD unless the operator sets one up. The experimental `aca` provider is the only sandboxing option documented: it relocates one agent's entire sub-loop (agentic loop, built-in tools, MCP calls) into a remote Azure Container Apps dynamic-sessions custom-container pool via a host-side transport shim (`AcaRuntimeProvider`); the workflow-level loop still stays on the host. This requires Azure credentials, a provisioned ACA session pool, and the `[aca]` extra, and carries documented 'Known Gaps (Runner MVP)' capability carve-outs and a cost note.
evidence.worker_features: Static parallel groups and dynamic `for_each` fan-out; sub-workflow composition (including inside `for_each`) with templated `input_mapping`; `script` steps that run shell commands and route on exit code or parsed JSON stdout; `set` steps for deterministic Jinja2-evaluated context bindings (no LLM/subprocess); `mcp` steps that call MCP tools directly with structured envelope routing and zero prompt tokens; `terminate` steps with explicit success/failed status and a structured reason; per-agent or workflow-wide `reasoning.effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) translated per provider; auto-discovery and injection of `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`.github/copilot-instructions.md` into every agent prompt; human-in-the-loop gates rendered as Markdown with clickable file links and answerable in-dashboard or via `conductor gate respond`; max-iteration and timeout safety limits; `conductor validate` static checks for stale template references, missing inputs and undeclared dependencies before runtime; and a Fleet Manager TUI (plus non-interactive `conductor fleet list` / `conductor stop`) showing live status, tokens and cost, gate alerts, and step-level drill-down across every running conductor process.
evidence.structured_events: An internal `EventCallback` bus carries typed payloads (`agent_message`, `agent_reasoning`, `agent_tool_start`, `agent_tool_complete`, `agent_tool_output_truncated`, plus workflow/turn boundary events such as `workflow_started`); `--metadata` is merged into the `workflow_started` event. `--silent` returns a single JSON result for the run. OpenTelemetry tracing (opt-in via the `telemetry` extra) emits provider-independent spans for workflow/group/agent/step/tool lifecycles and unifies them with native provider spans for the Copilot, Claude and OpenAI providers into one trace tree, exportable to any OTLP collector (e.g. Jaeger); prompt/response content capture is off by default (`OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT`). The web dashboard consumes the same event stream for live DAG visualization and in-browser gate answering.

evidence.auth_model: Paperclip runs its own identity system, separate from the agents it orchestrates. Docs (docs.paperclip.ing/administration/cli-auth/): "Trusted (Local Development): neither flow is required; the CLI and browser already trust the loopback." For remote/authenticated mode: "The CLI stores the board API token (and the user id it resolves to) in the platform-appropriate config directory, keyed by `apiBase`," obtained via `paperclipai auth login` (device-code flow: server-minted challenge -> browser approval -> stored board API token). Users create "a real, named human account" within Paperclip itself; the credential is "never [allowed to] leave the browser or the CLI process that asked for it." evidence.summary: Zeroshot is a Rust-native CLI/SDK (v10.7.0, MIT) that turns a software-change goal into an explicit, caller-authored multi-agent graph: one worker implements, independent acceptance and code-review agents verify in parallel, failures route to bounded repair, and delivery (local/push/PR/ship) happens only after checks pass. It targets local execution (reusing native Codex/Claude/Copilot logins), a self-hosted Docker target, or a managed Zeroshot Cloud target, and records every transition to a durable SQLite run ledger with resumable cursor-based status/log streams. A Python SDK wraps the same protocol.
evidence.interface: CLI (`zeroshot run/list/status/watch/logs/attach/force-stop/ui/template/connection/target`), a typed async Python SDK (`the-open-engine-zeroshot`, wraps the same Rust executable per-wheel), an HTTP/OECP protocol for direct/hosted targets, and an experimental ACP agent mode (`zeroshot acp --profile local:NAME`). Graphs (`GraphSpec`) and runtime plans (`RuntimePlan`) are exact typed JSON documents, not prompt text.
evidence.auth_model: No separate Zeroshot account is required for local/direct execution. Each agent binding names harness (codex/claude/copilot) + provider + model + optional named connections. For local runs, Codex/openai, Claude/anthropic, and Copilot/github lanes 'reuse the harness's native login and configuration without inventing a connection' (docs/concepts/runtimes-and-connections.md, docs/getting-started/install.md). Non-native provider lanes (openrouter, bedrock, gateway, or any contained/hosted target) require explicit credentials stored via `zeroshot connection set <key> --field ...` (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, GATEWAY_API_KEY, COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN). Zeroshot Cloud is a separate optional target requiring its own `zeroshot target login cloud` browser sign-in; it is not required to use the tool locally.
evidence.isolation_model: Local target: 'the same-user trust boundary as running the harness CLI directly' — mutates the caller's existing Git worktree, runs as the current user, and relies on the harness's own sandbox/permission policy (Zeroshot inspects and defers to configured approval/sandbox rules before adding any bypass flag; explicit rules take precedence). Local verifiers' edit-restriction is instruction guidance only, not a filesystem boundary. Direct/hosted targets: 'Hosted Codex and Claude workers and verifiers always run with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox / --dangerously-skip-permissions' inside a disposable capsule, which is the actual isolation boundary there; hosted verifiers get disposable writable copies with real process/filesystem isolation. No per-worktree sandbox is documented for local mode beyond the harness's own.
evidence.worker_features: Authored graph primitives: step/verifier executable nodes plus seq/choice/par/loop/map/succeed/fail composition groups; par/map allow multiple concurrent writer agents sharing the run workspace (coordination is the graph author's responsibility, not automatic isolation). Runtime plans set per-node harness/provider/model/size/effort/sessionScope(execution|node_instance) and named connections; `--uniform-runtime-config` vs full `--runtime-config` for per-node differentiation. Built-in `software-change` template: worker -> parallel independent acceptance + code-review verifiers -> bounded repair loop on rejection -> optional Git delivery (local/--push/--pr/--ship) with PR-feedback and CI/conflict/merge-policy gating. Bounds (maxIterations etc.) are graph-authored and cannot be raised by model output.
evidence.structured_events: Yes. Every run has a public ID backed by a SQLite ledger; status and 'safe-log' events carry opaque resumable cursors (`zeroshot watch RUN_ID --after STATUS_CURSOR`, `zeroshot logs RUN_ID --after LOG_CURSOR`), so detaching a client or losing a terminal does not stop the controller. `zeroshot list`/`status` return JSON. Python SDK exposes `run.watch(after=cursor)` yielding events and `RunWaitTimeout` carrying a still-live run handle. UI (`zeroshot ui`) provides live/replay graph + transcript viewing over the same event stream.
evidence.tests_and_ci: Repo has a `tests/` top-level directory (subdirs `docs`, `tooling`) and `.github/workflows/{ci.yml,docs.yml,pr-policy.yml,release.yml,release-python.yml}`; the README displays a live CI badge (`github/actions/workflow/status/the-open-engine/zeroshot/ci.yml`). evidence.summary: Agent Orchestrator (AO) is a local desktop app + daemon (Apache-2.0, active, 12266 stars, pushed same-day) that lets a user run and supervise many coding-agent "workers" — one task, one agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, OpenCode, +25 more via native Terminal UI), one isolated Git worktree each — from creation through PR, CI and review to merge in a live Kanban, plus a project-level "orchestrator" agent for cross-task planning. It reuses each agent's own native sign-in (no bundled provider CLIs, no AO API key for core use) and gives each worker its own worktree. Its public programmatic surface (a thin-HTTP-client CLI with `ao spawn`/`ao session restore` and --json launch-result flags, plus an internal `/api/v1/events` CDC feed for UI sync) is documented far less richly than the Claude Agent SDK or `codex exec`: no MCP support, no confirmed headless/exec mode with structured event streaming, and no documented resumable-session-with-structured-output flow were found in the fetched docs. It fits C1 (native-auth reuse), partially fits C3 (worktree isolation, not sandbox/container), and clearly overlaps three named incumbents (claude-code's Agent/Workflow tools, worktrunk's worktree management, and codex exec) with its main non-duplicated value being a cross-harness GUI supervision layer through merge, not a programmatic capability gap. Per the C5 rule, this remains keep_but_compare/targeted_candidate — not adoption — pending an executed comparison of AO's worker+orchestrator+Kanban flow against this project's coordinator + owned worktrees + verification-stage pipeline on one bounded multi-writer change.

It does not bundle Claude Code, Codex, or other provider CLIs." https://orchestrator.inc/docs: "Your agent CLIs and source-control credentials remain your own; AO does not bundle provider CLIs." and "Connect Mobile is a separate, opt-in home-network listener protected by a connection password." Scope the C1 verdict: native-sign-in reuse is confirmed for local desktop/daemon operation only. AO Cloud (web/mobile/cloud-agent modes) is a hosted control plane on https://api.aoagents.dev requiring a WorkOS-backed AO organization account and a production GitHub App installation. Record that as a C1 penalty on the cloud path, not as an open gap.

Replace the C3 finding with: dual isolation model — Git-backed local workers get a per-worker branch + worktree (README: "For Git-backed work, AO gives the worker its own branch and worktree"; architecture.md: "Project sessions own isolated git worktrees; projectless standalone workers own AO-managed plain-directory workspaces"), while cloud sessions get a Docker container with a persistent per-session volume, with Azure VM / Coder provisioning present under cloud/. Replace the C2 finding with: AO exposes a thin-HTTP-client CLI covering session lifecycle (spawn with --prompt/--mode/--branch/--issue, send, ls/get/kill/restore/switch-agent), PR merge, agent review trigger/submit, preview and browser control, several with --json; internally it runs ACP/JSON-RPC typed controllers with prompt replay across daemon restarts and a CDC->SSE event stream. What AO actually lacks versus claude-agent-sdk-python or `codex exec` is a *published, versioned programmatic contract* (no SDK package, no documented stream-json exec mode), not the underlying resumability or structured events. Rate C2 as partial-fit-with-undocumented-surface rather than absent.

Do not state "no MCP support." Correct statement: MCP is not documented on the product docs pages, but the codebase first-classes MCP tool calls (`mcp_tool` activity kind with server, tool name, structured arguments and structured result; 47 `mcpServers` code hits across the ACP chatdriver, ports, reviewer adapters and frontend types). MCP servers are configured in the wrapped agent, and AO renders/records the calls.

Correct the C4 release evidence: latest stable release is v0.13.0 (non-prerelease, 2026-09-12) atop a continuous semver line from v0.2.0, with a v0.12.1–v0.12.12 patch series; nightly prereleases are layered on top. Release discipline is a positive C4 signal, not an unclear one.
Correct the maintenance numbers: 378 open issues and 398 open PRs (not 777 open issues). Reframe the backlog risk as an open-PR/review-throughput question.

The repo shows a headless Go daemon (backend/cmd/ao) that the CLI starts and drives without the desktop app; the Electron app is one client. This makes the central fit framing ("sits above, not alongside") and the C6 portability gap both overstated, and turns C6 from an unconfirmable GUI question into a runnable local check.
findings.evidence: docs/cli/README.md: "The `ao` CLI is a thin Go/Cobra client for the local Agent Orchestrator daemon"; "make sure the daemon is running first with `ao start` or by opening the desktop app" (two independent paths); "The daemon always binds 127.0.0.1"; `ao doctor` "Check config, data directory, DB-file presence, daemon state, `git`, and (on Darwin/Linux) `tmux`"; build recipe `cd backend && go build -o ./bin/ao ./cmd/ao`; a "Manual smoke test" section that runs `ao status --json`, `ao doctor`, `ao start`, `ao stop` with no app. docs/architecture.md line 3: "Agent Orchestrator is a long-running Go daemon ... A TUI session runs its agent inside a tmux/conpty runtime". Only the preview/browser panel is app-bound ("The AO desktop app must be open because Electron owns the `WebContentsView`"). findings.problem: The repo's own CLI reference documents roughly 35 product commands, each mapped to a documented daemon REST route, plus an SSE event stream with named event types already consumed by a second non-UI client (mobile over authenticated LAN REST/SSE) and an `ao events` CLI whose backend routes are already in place. The programmatic surface is far thicker than the packet states, so the conclusion that AO "may not support headless automation the project's Workflow tool already provides" is not supported by the evidence the packet itself could have read.
findings.evidence: docs/cli/README.md route table: `ao send` -> `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send`, `ao session ls` ("shows branch, PR, CI, review, unresolved threads, activity, and age"), `ao session kill/restore/exit-agent/resume-agent/switch-agent`, `ao review ls|trigger|cancel|submit`, `ao pr merge`, `ao pr resolve-comments`, `ao hooks <agent> <event>` -> `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/activity`, `--json` on switch-agent/agent-switch ls/status/doctor/project get/claim-pr; "Commands not yet exposed but with backend routes in place include `ao events ...` (over the CDC/SSE endpoint)". docs/architecture.md: "CDC --> Broadcaster", "Broadcaster --> SSE", "Subscribers -->|SSE| Clients", named events "SSE session.created" / "SSE session.updated", and "Mobile -->|Authenticated LAN REST/SSE| Controllers".

findings.claim: worker_features / fit: "No MCP or custom-tools support is documented on the fetched pages" used in the fit verdict as a gap ("no MCP support ... and no evidence of custom-tool injection"), with the open gap "MCP support is not addressed anywhere in the fetched docs".
findings.problem: Argument from absence in the wrong layer. AO's stated design delegates the agent runtime to the installed agent CLI, so MCP servers and custom tools come from the wrapped Claude Code/Codex session, not from AO; the repo also carries first-class MCP activity handling and an ACP (JSON-RPC) chat transport. "No MCP" is therefore neither established nor a capability gap against this project, and it should not carry weight in the fit verdict.

findings.claim: overlap_with_incumbents: "AO adds a cross-harness ... always-on Kanban supervision UI ... this is the one plausible non-duplicated capability (C5), but it is UI/desktop-app value, not a programmatic capability gap".
findings.problem: There is at least one non-duplicated capability that is programmatic, not UI: mid-task harness switching (Claude Code <-> Codex) that preserves the AO worker session and its worktree, driven by CLI/REST with an idempotency key and an optional structured handoff payload. Neither claude-code's Agent/Workflow tools, `codex exec`, nor worktrunk provides this. Per-session PR/CI/review state (`ao session ls`, `ao review trigger|submit`, `ao pr merge`, `ao session claim-pr`) is likewise CLI-exposed, not UI-only. The overlap conclusion therefore misidentifies the delta, and the comparison it names ("does AO's Kanban add anything the coordinator's usage accounting and verification stage do not") aims at the wrong axis.

Public builds, tests, and contributors must not depend on that checkout." Repo tree contains pricing/catalog and .github/workflows/pricing-catalog-validate.yml (listed in the packet itself).

corrections: Rewrite fit_with_native_workflow's premise: AO is a headless local Go daemon (backend/cmd/ao, binds 127.0.0.1, tmux/conpty TUI runtimes) with three clients — a Cobra CLI, an Electron desktop app, and a LAN mobile client. It can sit alongside this project's stack on a WSL2 host, not only above it; only the preview/browser panel requires the Electron window.

Replace "no documented headless/exec mode with structured JSON event streaming" with: AO exposes a documented loopback REST API (~35 CLI-mapped /api/v1 routes incl. POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send) and a CDC-backed SSE stream with named events (session.created, session.updated) already consumed by a non-UI client; what it lacks versus `claude --print --output-format stream-json` / `codex exec` is a one-shot stdout-streaming exec mode and a published event schema, not event streaming as such. `ao events` is documented as backend-ready but CLI-unexposed.

Drop "no MCP support" as a fit gap. AO delegates the tool surface to the wrapped agent CLI (which carries its own MCP servers) and records MCP tool-call activity per session (migration 0074_activity_kinds_mcp_and_auto_review.sql); it also ships an ACP JSON-RPC chat transport. Restate as: AO adds no MCP layer of its own because it does not need one.

Replace the overlap_with_incumbents conclusion that AO's only non-duplicated value is UI: the programmatically non-duplicated capability is cross-harness mid-task switching with worktree and session preservation (`ao session switch-agent`, `ao session handoff submit --file <64KiB JSON>`, `ao session agent-switch ls --json`) plus CLI-exposed PR/CI/review supervision (`ao session ls`, `ao review trigger|submit`, `ao pr merge`, `ao session claim-pr`). None of claude-code's Agent/Workflow tools, `codex exec`, or worktrunk provides these; worktrunk overlap on the worktree primitive itself still stands (wt is installed on this PC at $HOME/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/bin/wt).

Restate C3 as mode-dependent: local mode is worktree/branch isolation only (as the packet says); the hosted cloud mode has a real container/sandbox provisioning layer (Docker, Coder, createos providers). That distinction also changes the comparison against anthropics/sandbox-runtime.

Resolve the C1 open gap instead of leaving it: the cloud control plane is private and tenant-authorized with a validated pricing catalog, so cloud-agent modes are behind a hosted AO account — record a C1 penalty for cloud mode only; local mode reuses native Claude Code/Codex/GitHub sign-ins as claimed.

Keep the disposition at keep_but_compare / targeted_candidate (no executed comparison exists), but replace the named comparison with three runnable ones: (1) C6 + headless viability on this WSL2 host — `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator /tmp/ao-src && cd /tmp/ao-src/backend && go build -o /tmp/ao ./cmd/ao && AO_PORT=3037 AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/aorun.json AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/aodata /tmp/ao doctor && ... /tmp/ao start && /tmp/ao status --json && /tmp/ao agent ls` (the repo's own documented smoke test); pass means AO runs with no Electron/WSLg and the packet's C6 gap is closed. (2) C2 event surface — with the daemon up, `curl -N http://127.0.0.1:3037/api/v1/events` while running `ao spawn --agent claude --name probe` then `ao send`, and record whether the stream carries typed, session-scoped, replayable events sufficient to drive a verification stage, versus this project's `node .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs --latest` child receipts. (3) C5 non-duplication — run one bounded two-writer change through `ao spawn` x2 + `ao session ls` + `ao review trigger` + `ao pr merge`, including one `ao session switch-agent <id> codex` mid-task, against the same change run through the coordinator + owned worktrees + `.claude/workflows/review-changes.js`; score only (a) whether mid-task harness switching with a preserved worktree is reachable any other way here and (b) whether AO reports per-child model/effort/usage at all, since that is the project's required accounting and is absent from AO's documented routes.
